column1: # Sky-position regression corpus for the direction cascade: the
# canonical high-PM set (tier-1 Gaia) plus one pin per non-Gaia tier —
# Sirius/Vega for hip2_saturated (the Gaia-saturated bright set),
# Gl 863.1A for simbad (the cascade's bottom tier).
# Positions are at the J2016.0 scene epoch (CATALOG_SCENE_EPOCH). There is
# no longer an unpropagated row: every tier now advances its own solution
# to the scene epoch, which is what retiring the printed cell bought.
# - Gaia tier: the raw Gaia DR3 catalog ra/dec, whose native epoch IS
#   J2016.0 — so the cascade's propagation is a Δt=0 no-op here. These
#   rows therefore pin source-id selection, tier routing, and xyz
#   assembly (a wrong source or a sign flip shows up as tens of arcsec),
#   NOT the propagation formula. That formula (PM sign / cos delta /
#   Δt direction) is exercised by the 24.75-yr HIP2 tier below and
#   pinned independently against SIMBAD J2000 in direction-cascade.test.ts.
# - Sirius/Vega (hip2_saturated): van-Leeuwen-2007 J1991.25 PM-propagated
#   24.75 yr forward to J2016.0 — this DOES exercise the propagation.
# - Gl 863.1A (simbad): no Gaia source, and HIP 111293 is absent from
#   HIP2, so the bottom tier places it — SIMBAD's bibcoded J2000
#   coordinate (2MASS, 2003yCat.2246....0C) advanced 16 yr on SIMBAD's own
#   bibcoded PM (1368.0, 111.0 mas/yr, 2005AJ....129.1483L). RE-PINNED
#   DELIBERATELY when the printed cell retired, and the move is the point:
#   this row used to hold that cell UNPROPAGATED, and the new value is
#   49.2" away. That splits into two separate corrections — the printed
#   cell sat 27.3" from SIMBAD's J2000 place (~20 yr of this star's motion,
#   so the cell was never really J2000), and the remaining 22.0" is the
#   J2000 → J2016 propagation the tier now performs. Tolerance 1.0" states
#   the confidence of a 2MASS coordinate plus a literature PM, not the
#   build's reproducibility, which is exact.
# - xi UMa: WAS the athyg_printed pin, until its spine row's backfilled
#   source_id reached a Gaia row. It now routes tier 1 as a 2p
#   (position-only) anchor and this row pins that Gaia J2016.0 coord — worth
#   ~11" of staleness against the printed cell it left, its 730 mas/yr over
#   the 16 yr from J2000. The 2p fit is blended (ipd_frac_multi_peak 24 on a
#   ~2" pair), so the coord is the pair photocentre rather than A alone —
#   good to ~1", which is why it stays looser than the 0.5" Gaia rows above.
# NO ROW PINS THE tycho2 TIER, and not for want of trying: a tycho2-tier
# record is by construction one Gaia and HIP2 both miss, and not one of the
# 43 carries a HIP, a Gaia source_id or a proper name — the only three
# things `parseRef` can address a record by. HD 14039 (TYC 3694-2544-1) is
# the row that would go here, the tier's highest-PM member at 408 mas/yr
# and a 10.2" propagation off its 1991.07 / 1991.00 mean epochs. The tier's
# split-epoch propagation is pinned at unit level in
# ../distance/direction-cascade.test.ts instead. Reaching it from a corpus
# needs an `hd:` ref kind, and so an HD index built off the search index —
# the binary carries no HD column.
# lookup: hip where the spine row carries one. xi UMa's row carries HIP
# 55203, but that Hipparcos entry is the unresolved AB pair and xi UMa B
# holds its own record, so the row is addressed by proper name instead and
# its hip cell is left blank to keep the lookup unambiguous.
# total_pm_masyr is the published total proper motion (mas/yr). The
# current-epoch velocity test advances the star's BAKED J2016 position +
# BAKED vx/vy/vz through the same epoch-advance-pure function the runtime
# uses and checks the on-sky angular displacement equals total_pm × Δt —
# validating end-to-end that catalog.bin's space-motion velocity reproduces
# the star's real proper motion (a wrong tier / distance-scale / unit / sign
# would miss badly at a 34 yr baseline). Blank = skip (velocity magnitude
# not pinned for that row) — xi UMa's 2p Gaia row fits no PM at all, so its
# record bakes no velocity and there is nothing to advance. Gl 863.1A is the
# only row pinning the simbad velocity tier, off SIMBAD's bibcoded PM —
# which is the same 1368.0 / 111.0 the printed cell carried, so the tier
# swap moved this star's velocity not at all.
